blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust applied to Retail & Consumer Banking. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Retail banks fight on experience and cost per account: onboarding friction, service resolution and cross-sell precision decide share of wallet. The machinery underneath — decisioning, document intelligence, contact platforms — is where Dataq Software engineers advantage.

items: Credential stuffing, SIM-swap and social engineering beat static MFA; fraud losses concentrate in digital channels.
Account opening abandons at KYC and document stages; manual checks take days while fintechs approve in minutes. Drop-off concentrates exactly where policy risk is highest.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Cyber Resilience & Incident Recovery, AI Security & Model Protection from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Account opening and KYC, Payment disputes and exceptions, Contact-center resolution) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — KYC/AML directives among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Secure the models themselves: prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming.
Behavioral biometrics, step-up auth and device intelligence (account-takeover losses down 30-45%)

blocks.caption: Regimes shaping this capability
rows: customer due diligence with periodic refresh duties
strong customer authentication with friction trade-offs
ICT risk, incident reporting, resilience testing and third-party oversight obligations with supervisory scrutiny

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Banking & Financial Services level this capability reads as: third-party register, incident playbooks and control tests continuously evidenced (assessment preparation down from quarters to weeks). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
